newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Fort Bonifacio may redeem preferred shares.
newsitem.headline: Manila Fort Bonifacio may redeem preferred shares.

text.p: Fort Bonifacio Development Corp (FBDC) may start redeeming its preferred shares this year, FBDC officials said on Wednesday.

The company issued non-voting preferred shares worth 28.4 billion pesos to Bonifacio Land Corp and state-run Bases Conversion and Development Authority (Basecon) to initially finance the development costs.
The preferred shares have a redemption feature, but it has an open-ended date on when the company would buy back the shares.
FBDC vice president Luis Pangilinan said based on the actual and projected cashflow, the company can redeem all preferred shares within two to three years' time.
He said the company was thinking of redeeming about 2.0 billion pesos worth of shares early this year. The redemption price per share is yet to be determined by the board.
"We don't need this much capital at this time. We want our shareholders to realise a good return of their investments as early as now," he said.

FBDC president Ricardo Pascua said the FBDC was able to rake in 29 billion pesos in land sales since it started pre-selling lots last year. The company was expected to post a net income of over 1.0 billion pesos last year, the second year of its existence.
Pascua said the company had decided to defer its initial public offering plan to a latter date.
"We don't really need to resort to additional funding," he told reporters.
FBDC is developing a 214-hectare prime land at the edge of the Manila's Makati financial district into the country's newest city. The private sector consortium is led by Metro Pacific Corp.
